key_insight: A hybrid photon-atom architecture can combine long-range photonic connectivity with reusable atomic hardware to build fault-tolerant quantum computers with near-deterministic entangling operations.
engineering_relevance: This blueprint points to a scalable hardware path for MBQC-based quantum computing that reduces photon-generation overhead while keeping error correction compatible with realistic cavity-QED noise.
method: Use single 87Rb atoms in optical cavities to implement a symmetrized Duan-Kimble photon-atom CZ gate.
Generate and reuse atomic resources to create large photonic cluster states with effectively unrestricted connectivity.
Map the system onto the RHG lattice and evaluate fault tolerance under a hardware-aware asymmetric loss model.
evidence_signal: Abstract reports logical-memory simulations with a photon-loss threshold of about 2.6% per physical gate, corresponding to roughly 15% total loss per trajectory, and identifies Clifford operations as threshold-matching in the proposed scheme.
watch_item: The architecture depends on precise cavity-QED performance and managing correlated photon-atom loss/errors, which may be difficult to sustain at scale.
paper_title: Blueprint for a fault-tolerant compound photon-atom quantum architecture
